newsitem.title: GERMANY: Degussa head says EMU would help his firm.
newsitem.headline: Degussa head says EMU would help his firm.

text.p: German chemicals and metals group Degussa AG said on Wednesday that it would benefit greatly from the launch of Europe's common currency, the euro, as foreign exchange risk would diminish considerably.

In an interview with the CNBC television network, Degussa management board chairman Uwe-Ernst Bufe said that since the majority of business was being conducted in Europe, the currency union would benefit the group a great deal.
"We still have about 70 percent of our business in Europe, and if we have a monetary union, then the same situation would apply in all nations," Bufe said.

Europe's currency union is scheduled to begin on January 1, 1999 with as many of the 15 European Union member nations as can meet the strict entry criteria on budget deficits, government debt, inflation, currency rates and others factors.
Most major German companies have already said that they would benefit from the union and endorse it, so long as the new currency is strong.
